detail.title: 1. The table of contents: which one?
detail.where: the heading "Inner Signal App to the Rescue!"
detail.question:
Three fresh readers read only the contents, with 16 situations a reader comes with (a friend shaking and not responding, a week later the world still feels unreal, planning a ceremony), and said where they'd look first. On the contents as it is, the two readers guessed on 6 and 5 of the 16, and both would have stopped at beach morning glory and missed niacin when they wanted the trip to end. On A, a third reader guessed on 4, and its first pick was right for all 16 ([what each reader found](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/bad-trips-20261105/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h39-20261109/toc/RESULTS.md)).

A (my pick):
Inner Signal App to the Rescue!
When to Bring In Outside Help
    Call medics for:
    When Peer Support Isn't Enough
    Who to Contact, and When   [moved here from Get One Human Anchor]
Acute Medical and Neurological Rescue
    Active Seizure   [the emergencies come first now]
    MDMA: Jaw Tension Is the Magnesium Alarm
    Chest Pain and Injury
    Recent Oral Toxic Ingestion
    Suspected Serotonin Syndrome (SS)
        Recognizing serotonin toxicity
        Do this immediately when serotonin toxicity is reasonably suspected:
    If Someone Says "My Brain Feels Damaged": DMSO + Humic Acid First   [moved to the end of the medical part, leading into the remedies]
My Acute Rescue Hierarchy of Remedies   ["of Remedies" added]
    How I label the evidence   [no longer the parent of every remedy]
    Some Remedies Require More Caution   [moved before the remedies]
    Gut-Toxin and Parasite-Die-Off Tools   [each remedy group one level up]
        Zeolite and Ferment in ZHoly3O
        Actual Activated Charcoal
    Nausea Smoothers When the Person Wants to Preserve the Trip
        Coffee Cherry for Nausea and Brain Recharge
    Mental Stabilizers That Don't Abort the Trip
        Metta NMT Sniffer Makes the Trip Chill & Lovey!
        Humic Acid Brings Brain to Optimal Function
        Authentic Calming Essential Oils (or a Lime Peel)   [new: your notes, card OILS]
        DMSO   [moved next to humic acid]
        Syrian Rue Oil Makes the Trip Gentle & Sweet   [new: your notes, card RUE-OIL]
        Ocean Water to calm & protect the energetic field
        Shungite, Aged Ozonated-Charcoal Water, or Boiled Charcoal Water
    When the Goal Is to Stop a Psychedelic Trip   [now after the stabilizers, gentlest to strongest]
        Beach Morning Glory--Ipomoea pes-caprae
        A Final Trip Killer: Niacin (a Form of Vitamin B3)   [your two headings joined]
Tripsitting Yourself or Others   [your part heading split in two; your greeting still opens it]
    Psychological First Aid: The First Five Minutes
        Stillness or Movement?
    Grounding Menu: Choose One or Two Things   [moved up, next to first aid]
    Get One Human Anchor
        Alone at 3 a.m.
    For the Person Helping: Calm Anchor, Not Guru
        Do
        When the Content Turns Toward Harm
    No Rash Actions: Visions Are Not Commands
    When the Trip Feels Amazing: Euphoric Certainty
Shadow Work   [the other half of your part heading]
    Dealing With Sorrow: Missing Versus Sending Love   [the hard-content sections, before the reflective ones]
    Hand on Heart and Gratitude 🫶🏿
        Touch, Consent, and Compassion
    Demons, Jinn, Entities, and Shadow Forces
    Abuse Memories, Recovered Memories, and Certainty
    Dealing With Shadow Thoughts
        The Joker Poem
    (Re)defining "Bad Trip"   [the reflective sections, after the hard content]
    Spiritual ≠ "Getting Your Ass Kicked"
    The Other Bypass: Feeling Good Forever
After the Storm   [a part of its own]
    What Kind of Aftermath Is This?
    Bring in mental-health support when:   [moved here from the top, right after the aftermath list]
    Hang up the phone, get off the Healing Treadmill   [moved here]
Give the Session a Beginning and an End   [a part of its own, for next time]
Appendix: Additional Resources

Pro: who to call is in one place at the top; the emergencies come first; the remedies run from the evidence key and the cautions to the gentlest and then the strongest; the psychological part is two short parts, what to do in the moment and the shadow work; the days after and the next session each have a part of their own. Con: the biggest change to the order your post has, and the brain section no longer leads the medical part.

B (only what both readers found broken):
Inner Signal App to the Rescue!
When to Bring In Outside Help
    Call medics for:
    Bring in mental-health support when:
    When Peer Support Isn't Enough
    Who to Contact, and When   [moved here from Get One Human Anchor]
Acute Medical and Neurological Rescue
    If Someone Says "My Brain Feels Damaged": DMSO + Humic Acid First
    Active Seizure
    MDMA: Jaw Tension Is the Magnesium Alarm
    Chest Pain and Injury
    Recent Oral Toxic Ingestion
    Suspected Serotonin Syndrome (SS)
        Recognizing serotonin toxicity
        Do this immediately when serotonin toxicity is reasonably suspected:
My Acute Rescue Hierarchy of Remedies   ["of Remedies" added]
    How I label the evidence   [no longer the parent of every remedy]
    Some Remedies Require More Caution   [moved before the remedies]
    Gut-Toxin and Parasite-Die-Off Tools   [each remedy group one level up]
        Zeolite and Ferment in ZHoly3O
        Actual Activated Charcoal
    Nausea Smoothers When the Person Wants to Preserve the Trip
        Coffee Cherry for Nausea and Brain Recharge
    Mental Stabilizers That Don't Abort the Trip
        Metta NMT Sniffer Makes the Trip Chill & Lovey!
        Humic Acid Brings Brain to Optimal Function
        Ocean Water to calm & protect the energetic field
        Shungite, Aged Ozonated-Charcoal Water, or Boiled Charcoal Water
        DMSO
    When the Goal Is to Stop a Psychedelic Trip   [now after the stabilizers, gentlest to strongest]
        Beach Morning Glory--Ipomoea pes-caprae
        A Final Trip Killer: Niacin (a Form of Vitamin B3)   [your two headings joined]
(the rest as it is now)

Pro: fixes the remedies part and who to call, and nothing else moves. Con: the psychological part stays one run of 17 sections with the days after at the end of it, and "Bring in mental-health support when:" stays at the top, away from the aftermath list.

C: leave the contents as it is.
